messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the private control-plane breakout: proposing a regional 'exit-proxy' model to collapse multiple outbound paths into one per region. Agents would connect to one DNS name per region; control plane handles tenant routing, policy, and fallbacks.

sam: Short ask: list the biggest tradeoffs we should call out (cost, latency, IP ownership, ops complexity).

hiro: Two immediate concerns: 1) customers that require stable source IPs for allowlists, 2) cross-account peering vs relay for private traffic.

priya: Implementation modes I'm seeing: (1) Shared regional proxy in our VPC with tenant routing (low ops for us, higher IP-preservation cost), (2) Light-per-tenant proxy in customer VPC (preserves IPs, higher install/ops), (3) Hybrid - shared proxy + optional local SNAT agent for customers who need IP-preservation.

ashok: Cost note: dedicated IP per tenant in our VPC = EIP per tenant + ACL/route complexity. Shared proxy reduces EIP count but breaks IP-based allowlists unless we provide per-tenant NAT pools or customer-managed agents.

leah: Observability asks: we need token-level traces that include exit.region, exit.mode (shared/local), snat_preserved=true/false, and per-hop latencies. Also cost attribution per-tenant per-route.

maria: What should fallback look like on proxy failure? We need an automatic failover to hosted endpoints and a policy that defines acceptable latency increase. Also who owns the SLA?

sam: Proposed SLO: regional exit-proxy 99.9% with documented median failover time to hosted API. We'll publish expected latency delta and cost delta for routes that use the proxy.

hiro: Security: agents authenticate with short-lived mTLS certs issued by CP. Proxies must store key material in KMS/HSM and rotate keys. If local agents are used, we need a bootstrap flow (ACME-style or CP-signed certs).

priya: Rollout plan sketch: keep existing peering as default, introduce exit-proxy behind a feature flag, route a small % (e.g., 5-10%) of traffic from non-sensitive tenants to proxy in staging, validate metrics, then expand opt-in cohorts. I'll draft RFC + migration runbook.

ashok: Rollout checklist items I'll own: infra sizing + autoscaling, NAT pool sizing (if shared), EIP accounting, connection counts per tenant, stress tests for connection churn, chaos sim for proxy outage.

leah: UX: some customers will want a CNAME or their own domain pointing at the exit endpoint; we should document DNS patterns and cert expectations.

maria: For customers that must preserve source IPs (regulated), we offer two paths: (A) local SNAT agent they run in their VPC (opt-in), (B) dedicated NAT pool/EIP assigned in our VPC per customer (higher cost). We should default to shared proxy unless they request preservation.

sam: Compliance note: identity header over a reverse tunnel is attractive (less IP churn) but won't satisfy allowlist-only audits. IP-preservation path required for those customers.

hiro: Threat model items: man-in-the-middle risk for reverse tunnels, misrouted tenant traffic, identity spoofing. We'll require mTLS + per-tenant cert binding and per-request tenant signatures for sensitive flows.

priya: Example routing policy we can share with agents (YAML):

```yaml
route_policy:
  - match: "inference.v1/*"
    primary: "regional-proxy"
    fallback: "hosted-api"
    allowlist_ip_preserve: false
  - match: "admin.metadata"
    primary: "hosted-api"
```

maria: Ops question: does consolidating increase blast radius materially? If a regional proxy goes down, we rely on CP-hosted endpoints; need clear failover time and communication plan.

ashok: We'll keep capacity headroom + health checks and route-level failover. Also prepare per-region playbooks for failover to hosted endpoint.

leah: Observability additions: add egress.error_rate_by_route, per-tenant egress_bytes, per-proxy CPU/memory and nat_conn_count. Also make routing decisions visible in console.

deploy-bot: deploy: exit-proxy-v1 -> staging (us-west-2) :rocket:

maria: Next actions: Priya -> RFC + runbook; Hiro -> threat model & cert bootstrap; Ashok -> rollout checklist and capacity calc; Sam -> SLO & cost model; Leah -> observability and console changes. Check-in Wed 10:00 PT.

sam: I'll prepare a simple cost comparison (shared vs dedicated NAT pools) and expected egress transfer delta.

priya: I'll include an opt-in flow for customers who want local agents and a migration checklist for allowlist customers.

hiro: Add a DNS permutation note: let customers choose their own subdomain or use our regional hostnames; document TTL and failover caveats.

ashok: Also add a metric to track per-tenant concurrent connections for NAT sizing and limit alerts.

leah: I'll review the RFC once priya has a draft.

maria: Thanks all, capturing these in the RFC. Closing this thread for now but leave comments if anything major is missed.
